chapter: Music in the family, learning to play
title: His father's cornet playing and the Roosevelt Hotel fountain lounge
summary: Johnny Detroit admired his father's playing and had him substitute at the hotel's fountain grill; Hirsch describes the room layout.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: But your dad was the only one that played, huh?

My, uh, father was the only one that played. He played the Cronolet, and, uh, he played pretty, pretty good. In fact, Johnny Detroit had a great respect for him, a great admiration for him, and he played for him. I mean, uh, great admiration for him. Yeah. Uh, when Johnny went to New York, he was working on the fountain grill of the Rosefeld Hotel, and he asked my daddy to substitute for him playing his place, and he did for about six weeks, I think it was. And he was very elated the way my father played. He said, my daddy could play a ballad better than anybody I ever heard. He had a beautiful tone on the clarinet, on the cornet, and he played the cornet. It wasn't until later that he played, uh, that he went to trumpet. Yeah.
Well, where was this that he substituted for?
The fountain lounge. Well, it was later the fountain lounge of the Rosefeld Hotel. Forest Grill. Bailey's is there now.

You know where Bailey's is? On Brown Street. All right. At one time, the Rosefeld Hotel used to be right, right where it is, except that where they had the, in later years, became the fountain, fountain lounge, and the breakfast room for the, breakfast room or the fountain lounge was where Bailey's is now. In other words, they used to do, when Kellner was there, they used to, on weekends when they'd have a big crowd, he was playing in the fountain, in the fountain room, fountain room lounge, and uh, they would open up the other room down there for the overflow of the people. And there was a dance floor, uh, that was, uh, like a dance floor down there. I think it was a hardwood floor down there that they'd let them use as a dance floor. They would dance and then have the sound that was coming down there and they could dance down there. They'd be dancing down there, dancing up in the fountain lounge.
